title: Show HN: Kestrom – Byte-verifiable LLM edits, IFC decoding, and backdoor scans

excerpt: Edit a language model inside a range, and let anyone check, byte for byte, what changed and what did not. Fine-tuning, LoRA, merging and quantization can move the output at any position. After such an edit, the only way to know that "nothing else changed" is to evaluate everything again, and even then you only know it for the prompts you tried. In our runs on Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3-8B, a 4-bit quantization and a public fine-tuned derivative each left 0 of 150 greedy answers the same as the original's. Kestrom takes the other side. Each edit comes with a range that is read from the weights or from the decoding, not from what the editor claims, and a report that anyone can rebuild on their own machine and compare with cmp. original weights ──edit──▶ edited weights ──kestrom-verify──▶ report.json │ W every byte the same but the changed rows │ U0 the original equal to itself on this machine │ G1 every logit outside the range equal, bit for bit (row edits) │ G2 greedy output the same until the range is reached ▼ the receiver rebuilds report.json ─▶ same bytes Two packages: The checks that pass say which tier an edit is in. Kestrom does not blur them. Determinism (U0: the original model gives the same logits and the same greedy output twice on your machine) is checked by logits and measure, which run the original twice, and by compare, on the two outputs of the original you give it. If U0 fails, G1 and G2 in that report mean nothing. range and diff read only bytes. compare checks the output files you give it: write them yourself, running the original twice. For decode-time edits it checks the output against the events the decoding records, not that a loop or a condition was really there. Product scope: - Supported (enterprise evaluation / audit): kestrom-verify (Apache-2.0), kestrom audit, kestrom inspect (including mirror and disarm), kestrom ifc (control / firewall), kestrom kv + kestrom generate --rules (open, loopguard, phrase, add, ban), kestrom rules (fit, run…
